verdict: Most of what the outside audit says "held up" turns out to be true when tested properly, but the auditor itself tested very little of it. Only A8 and A11 fully, and A6 and A9 in part, rest on a check that fails when the code is broken on purpose, and the auditor's own logs contradict A5, A12, B8 and A9's sentence about missing values. My own 74 tests on made-up data (each shown to fail on deliberately broken code) confirm the claims on lookahead, the close, the sealed season, signs and orientation, score matching and the Rule B/HT scorers. They also found one loading defect to fix before Thursday: when two F1 calls get back the same snapshot in the same batch of 50 calls, that whole snapshot is dropped and logged under the wrong reason. Finding 2 is not "conservative": the code can pass a cell that the registered sentence fails, so A2 needs a dated amendment before Thursday.

defects.title: D1. Two F1 calls that get back the same snapshot, in one batch of 50 calls, drop that whole snapshot
defects.evidence: SC=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maxzipperman-code-value-finder/b9c56e87-0800-41c5-8af9-65d864ba269e/scratchpad/pe-preflight/claims. `cd $SC/mine && ../pys.sh -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -rA test_pe_mine.py -k defect` -> 'PASSED test_defect_two_calls_returning_one_snapshot_in_one_batch_drop_it', 'PASSED test_defect_the_same_data_gives_different_quotes_depending_on_the_batch_boundary'. These tests assert today's behaviour. Requests at 15:55 and 16:00 are both answered with the 15:55 snapshot. With the default batch of 50: 0 quotes, drops {totals_not_two_outcomes: 2}. With batch=1: 2 quotes, duplicate_snapshot 2, 1 bet. With the same two calls split across calls 49 and 50: 2 quotes kept. The cause: quote_rows groups 4 outcome rows, and _pair rejects them. The auditor's own logs show the same: price.txt 'A5_duplicate_returned_snapshot {"batch": 50, "bets": 0, "drops": {"totals_not_two_outcomes": 2}, "quotes": 0}' and price-extra.txt 'A5_shuffle_byte_equal {"equal": [true, false, true]}'. The report omitted both. How often: before about Sep 18, 2022 the API kept one snapshot every 10 minutes (sharp-markets/docs/PLAN.md line 49). `$SC/pys.sh $SC/collisions.py` (kickoff times only) -> 'CFB: 1,000 F1 calls before 2022-09-18; grid at :x5: 46 snapshots returned to 2+ calls (44 with all copies in one 50-call batch; 22 involve a 16:00 daily call)'; grid at :x0: 0; NFL: 0 either way. On the :x5 grid, the Saturday 16:00 daily call and the 15:55 close of noon-Eastern CFB kickoffs share a snapshot. Those games lose their close, and every game loses that morning's entry snapshot. The loss is logged as *_not_two_outcomes. Check of the fix: `$SC/pys.sh $SC/mine/batch1_fixture.py` -> 'results.csv identical: True / drops identical: True'.
defects.smallest_fix: Read F1 one call at a time: in run.run, call load_quotes(cfg, calls, cache, batch=1) (or set batch's default to 1 in quotes.py). The existing duplicate check in load_quotes then keeps the first copy and counts the rest as duplicate_snapshot. This fixes loading and changes no threshold, flag, grading or decision rule; record it in the dated amendment before Thursday. After the pull and before the run, count calls whose returned timestamp repeats. That needs timestamps only, no prices.

defects.title: D4. K3 has no tie rule: when two books tie for the most bets, row order picks the book removed, and the verdict can flip
defects.evidence: `... -k tie` -> PASSED: 60 DraftKings bets at +3 and 60 FanDuel bets at -1. In one row order top_book = draftkings, CLV without it -1, K3 kills. Reversed, top_book = fanduel, +3, no kill. The auditor's price-extra.txt A14_book_tie shows the same; the report omitted it.
defects.smallest_fix: The amendment states a tie rule, for example: remove each tied book in turn, and K3 kills if any removal leaves CLV at or below zero. Until then, check top_book_share for ties by hand.

defects.title: D5. The early 9-day cut (COARSE_MARGIN, finding 4) drops a quote that the registered 7-day window keeps, when a game is later moved earlier by more than 2 days
defects.evidence: `... -k finding4` -> PASSED. A day-0 snapshot lists kickoff on day 10, so it is cut early. for_the_amendment:
A dated amendment before Thursday (before any F1 price is seen) should do eleven things:
(1) Section 7, A2: say whether "20 or more bets" counts all bets (as written) or bets with a Pinnacle close (as coded). My constructed cells show the two readings disagree in both directions, so this is not a clarification. If the written reading stays, say that a counted season with no Pinnacle close is not above zero.
(2) Record the loading fix: F1 calls are read one at a time, so a snapshot returned to two calls is read once and counted as duplicate_snapshot. Before the fix, in a batch of 50, both copies were dropped as *_not_two_outcomes.
(3) State the score-matching bounds already in the code. NFL: same two teams, kickoff's Eastern date within 1 day, exactly one candidate. CFB: same two schools within 36 hours, nearest game. Names come from cfbfastR team_info plus mascot, otherwise the longest school-name prefix. Aliases exist for Washington and Oakland.
(4) State the early cut: a quote more than 9 days (7 days plus 2 days' margin) before the kickoff listed in its own snapshot is dropped. This can drop a quote from a game later moved earlier by more than 2 days.
(5) Give K3 a tie rule for the book with the most bets.
(6) Say what K2 does when no result is matched (today it never kills), and require reading the 'graded' count before any verdict.
(7) Finding 1: any other primary cell (NFL, or CFB spreads or moneylines) that reaches "act" earns only a paper forward test, registered before its first eligible game, with no money (decision 4).
(8) Name the statistics the code uses: the 95% ROI interval is mean ± 1.96 × game-clustered standard error and needs at least 2 graded bets; the one-sided p comes from the normal curve; the clustered standard error uses the k/(k−1) factor; thresholds are inclusive (1e-9 tolerance); H2 orders by gap, then price.
(9) Section 2: change "never loads 2026 scores" to "never uses" (or add the read filter).
(10) Section 4: "−115 or better" means decimal 1 + 100/115 = 1.8696 or more (not 1.87).
